claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component authors can change a component's internal design and include the state migration in the same release.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
The pulumi/examples repository contains an aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with v1, v2, and v3 programs and the migration code.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, which creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing a VPC would require replacing the security group too, because the security group refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
The modern AWSX component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
The resource trees show legacy AWSX v1 uses component types `awsx:x:ec2:Vpc`, `awsx:x:ec2:Subnet`, `awsx:x:ec2:InternetGateway`, and modern AWSX uses `awsx:ec2:Vpc`.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, modern AWSX removes those wrappers, and the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resource options accept a `stateMigrations` option for registering a migration callback, used together with an alias for the legacy component type.

A state migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that replaces it).
Pulumi uses the `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid.
The `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a modern AWSX stack skips the first migration, and after both have run the callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; this example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.

Before each upgrade, `pulumi preview` should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group; preview evaluates the migration without saving it, and the update saves the migrated state.
When a component registers its migration internally, users need not write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs it as part of the normal preview and update.
A Pulumi docs guide on component state migrations exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ and covers the callback contract.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during both previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
A Pulumi state migration callback must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN that is omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The state entries passed to a Pulumi component state migration callback use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
The Pulumi stateMigrations resource option reference page documents the callback API at a 'callback-api' anchor.
A Pulumi component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The Pulumi restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
